title: Handlebars
subtitle: Handlebars templates drive the function generator's fourteen-file output.

stats.label: function crates in the estate carry the generator's fingerprints

lede: FAFO Core and Function Forge had a gap I wanted closed: agents could call tools but could not add one, and every new capability meant a person wiring a crate into the gateway, the orchestrator and the result path by hand. I built Function Forge, a generator that lets an agent author a new function, and Handlebars is its template engine. The generator is a Rust crate exposed as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool. From one function specification (name, parameters, data source, flags) it renders a crate. One flag reshapes the generated code for a function that submits GPU inference work and exits, with routing by model id enforced.
quote: Templates own everything structural and authors write only inside a bounded zone, which keeps agent-written code inside the platform's write-path architecture.
evidence: Code generation and metaprogramming: a Rust generator exposed as an MCP tool that renders a function crate from one specification, with fixed framework files and a sandboxed developer zone.

Tool synthesis under governance: one operation that wires gateway, control plane and completion service with rollback and link-time registration; 7 of 14 function crates carry the generator's fingerprints.
author: Corey James
